chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Malik al-Nahwi reported to me from Muhammad ibn al-Fadhl, by his former chain of narrations till al-Asma'i, from Isa ibn Umar, who said:

A man once sought help from Abu Amru ibn al-Ala' for his needs and Abu Amru promised him. But then, it became impossible for Abu Amru to fulfil the promise. Later, the man said: "O Abu Amru, you promised me but never fulfilled it!" Abu Amru said: "Who deserves more grief, you or I?" The man said: "I." Abu Amru said: "No, by Allah, rather I do." The man asked: "How so?" He said: "Because I promised you, so you went away with the joy of the promise, and I went away with the worry of fulfillment. You slept happy and delighted while I spent my night thoughtful and anxious. Then circumstances prevented me, so you met me ashamed and I met you humbled."
ai.seo_question: What did Abu Amru ibn al-Ala say about the burden of broken promises?
ai.summary: This narration captures Abu Amru ibn al-Ala's eloquent response when confronted about an unfulfilled promise. His reply illustrates a profound ethic of promise-keeping: the one who promises bears a greater burden of distress than the one waiting, because the promiser carries both the anxiety of fulfillment and the shame of failure. The story highlights how broken promises weigh more heavily on the conscience of an honorable person.
